description:
FILED s536e (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08) beside #4547 (scratch/s536e/pr/m1g.pl in the s536e worktree).

REPRODUCER (probed vs perl 5.40.3):

    my %ENV = (k => 1); package Q; print join(",", keys %ENV), "\n";

perl:              k
base c8886b61:     the whole process environment (LESSOPEN,PERLBREW_VERSION,...)  -- SILENT WRONG
s536e:             Transpile failed: Parser2 TODO: my-lexical 'ENV' (canon %ENV) spans a package boundary   -- LOUD

WHY: the span pass's container half (W10-ext-3, `_span_rename_containers`) promotes a container under its OWN name only (identity); for an exception-partition name that symbol is the runtime's special (%ENV, @ARGV ...), and the exception rename (#296) then moved the declaration off it, so the later section's qualified `%main::ENV` read the real environment.  s536e's `_own_name_cell_ok` (the one identity predicate) now refuses identity for an exception name, so the container is not promoted and the checker refuses.

FIX DIRECTION: give the container span path the MANGLE the scalar path has (`%ENV__file__N`: rename the declarator with `_rename_decl_within`, the declaring segment's later uses bare, the later segments' qualified), so an exception-named or #470-named container spanning a section promotes.  Rare (a file-level `my %ENV` across a `package` statement).  Name-resolution change: the sweep is the gate.

=== DONE (s537b) -- the container span path gets the MANGLE (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-11, generation v2-13800; = #338 b1) ===
Every spanning CONTAINER binding is promoted on its own (Parser2 `_span_container_instances` / `_span_rename_container` / `_span_rewrite_container_stmt`): IDENTITY where its declaration is the canon's only one file-wide, `_own_name_cell_ok` and a program unit (unchanged); else the scalar path's MANGLE `@x__file__N` -- the declarator renamed alone (`_rename_decl_within`, binder-exact), the declaring section's later uses bare, later sections' qualified, interpolated text everywhere; `_span_check_rewritten` (rule 12) and the eval pair (`_publish_span_pair`) as for scalars.  Chained / embedded container declarators are offered like #4425's scalars (their statement publishes the cell, `_emb_promoted`); the chain lowering in `_lower_decl_list` lets only the unpromoted names.  #4661 (`my %ENV` / `my @ARGV` / `my %SIG` across a section), #4662 (`my @c = my @d = ...`, `push(my @e, ...)`, `my ($x, %h); { my %h }`, op/svleak.t's three `my @a`) -- probes scratch/s537b/pr/m3[a-h].pl perl -> base (refused every one) -> tree = perl.  Guards Pl/t/span-binder-01.t rows 36-37, fail on the base.
DIRECTION D (#338 b1's open question) MEASURED: the identity spelling with a nested `p-let` of `@a` under `p-defcell @a` (hand-edited emission, scratch/s537b/m3h-id.lisp) prints perl's answer -- a `let` of the symbol-macro name shadows it, no poison.  The mangle is chosen for ONE rule with the scalar path (decl_count > 1 / exception name / non-program unit), not for safety.
Still refusing (loud): a container spelled `${x}`-braced anywhere in the file, a block-form section's decl.  Found beside it, pre-existing: #4822 (a bare `%h` inside `"@{[ ]}"` is no use to the binder or the interp fixer).
subject: A FILE-level `my` of an EXCEPTION-partition CONTAINER (`my %ENV`, `my @ARGV`, `my %SIG` ...) used in a later `package` section is REFUSED "spans a package boundary" since s536e -- before it the later section silently read the REAL %ENV
